# wake v0.2.0

WAKE is now state-aware instead of blindly sending continuation prompts every
quarter hour.

## Main fix

When Codex is waiting for the user to answer, approve, provide credentials,
restart something, or complete another manual step, WAKE now classifies the
conversation as `WAITING_USER` and pauses its own schedule.

This prevents the repeated pattern:

```text
09:00 continue...
09:15 continue...
09:30 continue...
09:45 continue...
```

while the conversation is simply waiting for the same user action.

## State machine

- `ACTIVE` — work is already progressing; do not duplicate it.
- `WAITING_USER` — pause WAKE until the user responds.
- `RETRYABLE_BLOCKED` — keep the schedule for quota/rate/network/service retry.
- `RUNNABLE` — continue unfinished work.
- `DONE` — remove WAKE.
- `UNKNOWN` — ask once, then pause.

## Re-arm

When the user returns and resolves the blocker, WAKE can re-enable the existing
schedule. The skill allows implicit invocation only for this re-arm path.

If implicit re-arm is not selected by the host/model, run:

```text
$wake
```

## Supervisor note

Codex App Server has promising primitives for a future single cross-thread
supervisor, including non-resuming thread reads and user-input/approval events.
v0.2 intentionally does not enable that backend by default because reliably
attaching an external process to the exact live Codex Desktop thread is not yet
a generally documented/safe integration boundary.

## Safety

WAKE does not bypass OpenAI quotas, usage limits, rate limits, or safety controls.
